markscheme: M1: $10\%$ of £80 $=$ £8 and used to build $35\%$ (or equivalent non-calculator strategy)
questions.modelAnswer: $10\%$ of £80 is £8, so $30\%$ is $3 \times 8 = 24$ pounds and $5\%$ is half of £8, which is £4. Add: $24 + 4 = 28$. Answer: £28.

markscheme: B1: $4$ identified as the highest common factor and taken outside the bracket
questions.modelAnswer: The highest common factor of $8$ and $12$ is $4$. Taking $4$ outside the bracket: $8x + 12 = 4(2x + 3)$. Check: $4 \times 2x = 8x$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$ ✓

markscheme: B1: $4.5$ seen as the number between $1$ and $10$
questions.modelAnswer: Move the decimal point $4$ places to get a number between $1$ and $10$: $45\,000 = 4.5 \times 10\,000 = 4.5 \times 10^{4}$.

markscheme: M1: $3x = 15$ (collecting the $x$ terms on one side and constants on the other)
questions.modelAnswer: Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $3x - 4 = 11$. Add $4$ to both sides: $3x = 15$. Divide by $3$: $x = 5$. Check: $5(5) - 4 = 21$ and $2(5) + 11 = 21$ ✓

questions.stem: Work out the size of one interior angle of a regular hexagon.
markscheme: M1: $(6 - 2) \times 180$ (interior angle sum of a hexagon)
questions.modelAnswer: The interior angles of a hexagon sum to $(6 - 2) \times 180 = 720^\circ$. A regular hexagon has $6$ equal angles, so each angle is $720 \div 6 = 120^\circ$.

questions.stem: A bag contains $3$ red counters and $5$ blue counters. Two counters are taken out at random, one after the other, without replacement. Work out the probability that both counters are red.
markscheme: M1: $\dfrac{3}{8}$ for the first red counter
M1: multiplying by $\dfrac{2}{7}$ for the second red counter (without replacement)
questions.modelAnswer: P(first red) $= \dfrac{3}{8}$. One red is removed, leaving $2$ red out of $7$, so P(second red) $= \dfrac{2}{7}$. Multiply along the tree: $\dfrac{3}{8} \times \dfrac{2}{7} = \dfrac{6}{56} = \dfrac{3}{28}$.

questions.stem: A ladder of length $13$ m leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is $5$ m from the base of the wall. Work out how far up the wall the ladder reaches.
markscheme: M1: $h^{2} + 5^{2} = 13^{2}$ (Pythagoras applied to the right-angled triangle)
questions.modelAnswer: The wall, ground and ladder form a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $13$. By Pythagoras: $h^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2} = 169 - 25 = 144$. So $h = \sqrt{144} = 12$. The ladder reaches $12$ m up the wall.

questions.stem: A cuboid measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm by $3$ cm. Work out its total surface area.
markscheme: M1: three different face areas found: $20$, $12$ and $15$ cm$^{2}$
questions.modelAnswer: The three different faces have areas $5 \times 4 = 20$, $4 \times 3 = 12$ and $5 \times 3 = 15$ cm$^{2}$. Each face appears twice, so the total surface area is $2 \times (20 + 12 + 15) = 2 \times 47 = 94$ cm$^{2}$.
